From: dylan_brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>

Cc: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-03 09:52 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden p95/p99 jumps this morning

Quick update from infra debugging:
- No config rollouts or kernel swaps in the window.
- We observed a change in request shape: a subset of requests with longer context lengths pushed batch formation time out, causing longer batching wait windows and increased queue depth.
- Autoscaler did not trigger additional nodes because CPU and GPU utilization per instance were below scale thresholds — the system misattributed latency to batching and kept batching aggressively which amplified tail latencies.

Immediate mitigation I'm pushing now: reduce max batching window for the affected pool and enforce a hard cap on batch size to limit batch formation delay. Going to throttle batch wait from 40ms -> 15ms and cap size at 12. Rolling now (ETA 6–8 mins).

— Dylan
SRE
From: aisha_rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Jen Li <jen.li@bluefinhealth.com>

Date: 2027-10-03 10:05 -0700
Subject: Re: sudden p95/p99 jumps this morning

Jen — we rolled a temporary mitigation (reduced batching window + hard batch cap) and are seeing p95 stepping down in our internal metrics. We're keeping Bluefin traffic pinned to the mitigated pool for the next 2 hours while we collect stable traces. Expect 10–15% improvement in p95 within 10 minutes of the roll.

Next steps we propose:
1) Stabilize with current cap and monitor for 24h.
2) Rishi to review batching heuristics so we avoid misattributing long-context requests to batching waits.
3) Mutual action plan draft attached for internal/external sign-off that outlines detection rules, capacity thresholds, and longer-term runtime changes.

We understand the impact and will follow through until this is fully closed.

— Aisha

Date: 2027-10-05 17:43 -0700
Subject: Follow-up: deep dive & long-term prevention plan

Two days post-incident: summary and recommended actions.

What happened (recap):
- A minority of long-context requests increased batch formation latency. Because batching parameters favored larger batches to optimize throughput, waiting windows lengthened and queue depth climbed. This produced a cascading tail-latency effect and introduced intermittent 502s when internal queue thresholds were breached.

Short-term changes implemented:
- Reduced max batching window and enforced a conservative batch-size cap (temporary).
- Pinned Bluefin traffic to mitigated pool while we validate.

Longer-term fixes (proposal):
1) Context-aware batching: detect long-context request patterns and isolate them to smaller, dedicated batch lanes to avoid penalizing short requests.
2) Autoscaler tuning: include queue depth and batch wait time as scale signals (not just utilization).
3) Runtime telemetry: add a batching wait histogram in the console and an alert when median wait > 20ms or when an instance queue exceeds 75% configured depth.
4) Post-incident follow-up: 1-week monitoring SLA for Bluefin and a joint runbook sign-off (attached mutual_action_plan_v1.xlsx).

I'll set up a short architecture review with product + infra this week to scope effort. ETA for context-aware batching prototype: 6–8 weeks.

Action items:
- Aisha: confirm Bluefin is OK with the proposed runbook and the 1-week monitoring SLA.
- Marissa: collect any remaining traces from Bluefin and drop into the shared Drive link.
- Dylan: scope autoscaler signal changes and put a low-risk rollout plan in the ticket.

Thanks everyone — we'll coordinate the next call once Bluefin signs the mutual action plan.

— Rishi
Director, Product (Serving Runtime)
Redwood Inference
